title: Janmashtami 2026: Puja Timings, Muhurat, and Where NRIs Can Celebrate
excerpt: Krishna Janmashtami falls on September 4 this year, with ISKCON temples across the US hosting midnight arati, kirtans, and free prasadam for the diaspora.
body:
• Krishna Janmashtami falls on Friday, September 4, 2026 — both Smarta and ISKCON/Vaishnava traditions converge on the same date this year
  • Nishita Puja muhurat spans approximately 11:57 PM to 12:43 AM (Delhi), with Ashtami Tithi running from 2:25 AM on September 4 to 12:13 AM on September 5
  • Nandotsav and Dahi Handi celebrations follow on Saturday, September 5
  • ISKCON temples across the US are hosting major celebrations in Boston, Milpitas, Dallas, Round Rock, and Laguna Beach with midnight arati and free prasadam

Millions of Hindus worldwide mark Krishna Janmashtami on Friday, September 4, celebrating the 5,253rd birth anniversary of Lord Krishna. In a relatively rare convergence, both Smarta and ISKCON/Vaishnava traditions observe the festival on the same date this year, followed by Nandotsav and Dahi Handi celebrations on Saturday, September 5.

Puja Timings and Muhurat

The Ashtami Tithi begins at 2:25 AM on September 4 and ends at 12:13 AM on September 5, according to Drik Panchang. Rohini Nakshatra — considered the most auspicious time for Krishna's birth — runs from 12:29 AM to 11:04 PM on September 4.

The Nishita Puja muhurat, the midnight window when Krishna is believed to have been born, varies by city:

  • Delhi: 11:57 PM to 12:43 AM (September 5)
  • Mumbai: 12:14 AM to 1:01 AM (September 5)
  • Chennai: 11:45 PM to 12:31 AM (September 5)

Devotees observing a fast can break it (Parana) after approximately 6:00 AM on September 5, once the Ashtami Tithi and Rohini Nakshatra have both concluded.

Celebrations Across the US

For the Indian diaspora in the United States, ISKCON temples and Hindu mandirs are hosting large-scale celebrations from coast to coast. Several have moved to bigger venues to accommodate growing attendance.

ISKCON Boston is hosting celebrations from 4:00 PM to 11:00 PM at Emmanuel Church on Newbury Street — a larger venue than the usual temple — with a midnight arati at the ISKCON Boston center on Commonwealth Avenue. Sri Krishna Balaram Mandir in Milpitas, California, opens at 5:00 PM with Go Puja (cow worship), Maha Abhisheka, a Kids Mela, and free prasadam through midnight.

"Come, celebrate Lord Sri Krishna's Appearance Day with us! Join us for an uplifting evening filled with kirtan, dance, and delicious prasadam."

— ISKCON Boston

The Radha Krishna Temple of Dallas is hosting a four-day Janmashtami Mahotsav from September 3 through 6, featuring kirtans, a Dahi Handi celebration presented by Maharashtra Mandal, a fancy dress competition, and a food festival — all in the presence of Swami Mukundananda. In Round Rock, Texas, ISKCON is running three days of festivals starting September 4, including a calf meet-and-greet, cultural performances, and a "Dress for Damodar" costume parade for children.

In Southern California, the Sri Krishna Janmashtami event in Laguna Beach features mantra music, cultural performances, and a free vegetarian feast with complimentary shuttle service from Laguna Beach High School.

Traditions and Significance

Janmashtami commemorates the birth of Lord Krishna in Mathura, believed to have taken place at midnight. Devotees observe a day-long fast, decorate temples and homes, sing bhajans and kirtans, and perform an abhishek (ritual bath) of Krishna idols with milk, curd, honey, and ghee. The midnight arati — marking the exact moment of Krishna's birth — is the spiritual centerpiece of the celebration.

Nandotsav on September 5 celebrates the joy of Nanda Baba upon learning of Krishna's birth. In Maharashtra and parts of the US diaspora, this takes the form of Dahi Handi — where teams form human pyramids to break an earthen pot of butter suspended overhead, recreating young Krishna's legendary butter-stealing antics.

Where to Celebrate

Indian community members looking for celebrations near them can check local ISKCON centers, Hindu temples, and community organizations. Most events offer free entry and prasadam, with activities for families and children. The festival provides one of the year's largest gathering points for the Indian diaspora, drawing thousands to temples across major metropolitan areas.
